# Requirement-to-Concept Trace

| Requirement                                       | Concept                            | State/behaviour                                                                                        | Decision                                                                               |
|---------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| FR-01 Create patient record                       | Patient                            | Patient identity fields are directly stored when the record is created.                                | Patient class directly stores the required identity information                        |
| FR-02 Create practitioner record                  | Practitioner                       | Practitioner identity and specialty details are stored when the record is created                      | Practitioner class directly stores the required practitioner information               |
| FR-03 Book appointment                            | Appointment, Patient, Practitioner | A new appointment links a patient and practitioner to a selected date and time                         | Appointment class stores references to the associated Patient and Practitioner         |
| FR-04 Prevent duplicate/clash                     | Practitioner, Appointment          | Incoming booking time is always checked against the practitioner's existing appointments for conflicts | It remains as a workflow validation rather than being joined with appointment class    |
| FR-05 Cancel appointment                          | Appointment                        | Appointment status changes from booked to cancelled while the record remains available                 | Appointment manages its own cancellation behavior through a status change              |
| FR-06 Retain cancelled history (30 days)          | Appointment                        | Cancelled appointments remain stored in the system instead of being deleted                            | Cancellation is modelled as a status change so the appointment history can be retained |
| FR-07 Search patient by name/ID                   | Patient                            | Existing patient identity fields are compared with the entered search term                             | Search logic sits outside the Patient class rather than being in it                    |
| FR-08 List practitioner appointments/availability | Practitioner, Appointment          | Appointments are filtered or grouped according to the selected practitioner                            | Uses the Practitioner–Appointment association to access the relevant appointments      |
| FR-09 Update appointment status                   | Appointment                        | Appointment status changes between the allowed status values based on the relevant action              | Appointment controls its own status transitions                                        |
| FR-10 View patient appointment history            | Patient, Appointment               | Existing appointments are filtered or grouped according to the selected patient                        | Uses the Patient–Appointment association to retrieve the patient's appointment history |
| FR-11 Duplicate/clash error message               | Appointment, Practitioner          | A booking attempt is checked for a scheduling conflict before it is accepted                           | Uses the same underlying duplicate/clash validation as FR-04                           |
| FR-12 Generate report by date range               | Appointment                        | Existing appointment records are filtered and summarized according to the selected date range          | Treated as a reporting/query function outside the core domain classes                  |

# Design Rationale

Explain class selection, responsibility allocation and key
relationships.  
  
Patient, Practitioner, and Appointment are the only classes justified by
the confirmed FR-01 to FR-12 and each has its own identity, state, and
behavior that is tied directly to a requirement. Database, Cancellation,
Status and Report were rejected as domain classes because they are
infrastructure, state transitions, enumerated values or query outputs,
respectively, not independent domain concepts.  
Responsibility allocation follows FR ownership: Patient owns
identity/validity (FR-01, FR-07), Practitioner owns its own
identity/specialty (FR-02), and Appointment owns the booking state and
legal state transitions including cancellation and status updates
(FR-03, FR-05, FR-06, FR-09). The FR-04/FR-11 duplicate-conflict check
spans multiple appointments for one practitioner, so it is deferred to a
later workflow/service responsibility rather than forced onto a single
Appointment object.  
Patient \<-\> Appointment and Practitioner \<-\> Appointment are
modelled as associations, not composition, because Patient and
Practitioner exist independently of any one Appointment; cancelling or
deleting an Appointment must not destroy its linked Patient or
Practitioner.

# AI Design Review Record  

Prompt used -Using only the confirmed SmartCare requirements below, suggest candidate domain classes, responsibilities, and relationships. For every suggestion, cite which requirement supports it. Do not invent features, database concerns, or UI details. Flag anything uncertain separately for human review.


| AI suggestion                                            | Evidence                                                                                         | Decision     | Reason                                                                                       | Model change                                                                                                          |
|----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Include a **Patient** class                              | FR‑01 (create patient), FR‑07 (search patient), FR‑10 (view history)                             | Accepted     | All three requirements explicitly require patient records and history                        | Patient class added with minimal attributes (name, contact details)                                                   |
| Include a **Practitioner** class                         | FR‑02 (create practitioner), FR‑03 (booking), FR‑08 (availability), FR‑04 (double‑booking rules) | Accepted     | Practitioner is required for booking, availability, and clash prevention                     | Practitioner class added with minimal identity attributes                                                             |
| Include an **Appointment** class                         | FR‑03–FR‑12 (booking, cancellation, retention, status, history, clash errors, reporting)         | Accepted     | Appointment is central to almost all requirements                                            | Appointment class added with patient, practitioner, time, status                                                      |
| Appointment should link **Patient** and **Practitioner** | FR‑03 (booking involves both), FR‑10 (patient history), FR‑08 (practitioner schedule)            | Accepted     | Relationships are explicitly required for history and availability                           | Appointment → Patient and Appointment → Practitioner associations added                                               |
| **Add AppointmentStatus as a separate concept as Enum**  | FR‑09 (update status: completed, cancelled)                                                      | **Modified** | Status changes are required, and separating status avoids mixing logic with appointment data | Status added as a plain string attribute on Appointment with valid values noted in a comment                          |
| Add **AppointmentHistory / RetentionPolicy**             | FR‑06 (retain cancelled for 30 days), FR‑10 (full history)                                       | Modified     | History retention is a real requirement, but a standalone class is not yet justified.        | Retention is modelled as a status value on Appointment (CANCELLED), with cancelled appointments retained and not deleted. |
| Add **SearchService** (domain‑level responsibility)      | FR‑07 (search patient), FR‑08 (list practitioner appointments)                                   | Modified     | This is a real requirement but giving it a name as a Service class is early for this stage   | Search will be as required behavior and will not be introduced as a class yet                                         |
| Add **ReportingService**                                 | FR‑12 (generate basic report)                                                                    | Modified     | This is a real requirement but giving it a name as a Service class is early for this stage   | Reporting will be as required behavior and will not be introduced as a class yet                                      |
| Add **TimeSlot / Availability** for practitioners        | FR‑08 mentions “availability” but does not define structure                                      | Uncertain    | Requirement does not specify how availability is represented                                 | Flagged for human review; not added to model yet                                                                      |
| Define detailed contact‑details fields                   | FR‑01 only says “contact details”                                                                | Rejected     | No requirement specifies phone/email/address                                                 | The model keeps contact details generic                                                                               |
| Define detailed practitioner attributes                  | FR‑02 only says “practitioner record”                                                            | Rejected     | No requirement specifies fields beyond identity                                              | Model keeps practitioner minimal                                                                                      |
| Define report format or structure                        | FR‑12 only says “basic report”                                                                   | Uncertain    | No requirement defines output format                                                         | Report format left is not yet decided but reporting behaviour is noted as required and not yet formalized as a class  |
